title: Round-Robin Arbiter
constraints: `grant` is registered: at each rising edge it becomes the one-hot grant for the `req` sampled at that edge, or 0 if `req == 0`.
A pointer holds the requester with the highest priority. The search goes `ptr, ptr+1, …` (mod 4) and the first active request wins.
After granting requester i, the pointer moves to `(i + 1) mod 4`. With no requests the pointer does not move.
hints: Rotate `req` right by `ptr`, run a simple fixed-priority (lowest bit wins) search, then rotate the result back.
Or double the request vector: `{req, req} >> ptr` puts the candidates in priority order.
Keep `ptr` as a 2-bit counter so wrap-around is free.

examples.title: pointer skips idle requesters
examples.expected: grant = 1000 (requester 3 is next in the rotation), then 0001
